headline: Models predict unmeasured expression, protein and 3D gene fields from histology and sparse spatial data
label: Inferring Unmeasured Expression
summary: New preprints infer unmeasured RNA, protein and 3D expression from H&E, sliced spatial data and transcript geometry, alongside perturbation and embedding methods.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting molecular readouts that were not directly assayed. SCOPE predicts single-cell RNA and protein levels from H&E using RNA-protein biomarker priors, reporting improved Pearson correlation across 16 organs. HoloGene lifts pre-registered spatial slices into continuous 3D gene-expression fields with an anisotropic conditional implicit neural representation. A rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds and improves protein prediction. scPACE imputes missing cell states in cohort data. A second strand concerns perturbation and signaling: OCCAM predicts perturbation effects, and CIRCE infers graded signaling activity from combinatorial perturbation structure. Representation work includes scUNVEIL's next-UMI pretraining on about 92M cells, GatorAnchor's uncertainty-aware neighborhoods, and CIRCA's identifiable cell and niche programs. Spatial multi-omic modeling (multiCAsp) and domain detection (CASTLE) are adjacent rather than inference-focused.
